claim_reviews.conclusion: “Last week” and “the week immediately before the current week” are correctly aligned.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Minggu lalu” is a correct and ordinary Indonesian expression for last week.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian form

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Minggu lepas” is a standard and commonly attested Malaysian Malay expression for last week.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian form

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is acceptable as a preference contrast, provided it is not interpreted as exclusivity; Malaysian Malay also permits “minggu lalu.”
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false friend is present; “lalu” and “lepas” function here as temporal equivalents.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both target forms correctly express “last week.” “Minggu lalu” is standard Indonesian, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “minggu lepas”; “minggu lalu” is also possible in Malaysian usage. The relation is a valid common-word preference contrast, not an exclusive national distinction. No false-friend issue is present.
